newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury's Summers - economy strong, inflation low.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury's Summers - economy strong, inflation low.

text.p: The U.S. economy is strong and rising wages have not pushed up inflation, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said Thursday.

"Wages are rising, at a 3.9 percent annual rate, but with no indication that inflation is starting to heat up as a result," Summers said in a prepared speech for an Ernst & Young tax conference in New York, that was released here.
He added that the United States is enjoying a "low-inflation, investment-led recovery."

The economic recovery appears to be on middle ground, Summers said. "So far, our recovery seems in the middle of the fairway, about midway between the rough of an economic slowdown and the rough of overheating," he said.
America's weakness lies in its low savings rate relative to other countries, Summers said.
"Yet if there is an Achilles heel to our future security, it may be our weak level of savings relative to many countries," he said.
The prospects for stability in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union have much to do with those regions making a successful transition to market economics and prosperity, Summers said.
The international financial institutions are playing a central role in guiding Russia and other former Soviet Union nations to market-based prosperity, he said.
"If Russia's efforts run into turbulence, it will be because substantial, credible support was not provided during what could have been the most propitious period," he said.
"The multilateral development banks are leveraged ways for America to accomplish its economic security objectives," he added.
